reference: (a) published Fe-Fe3C invariant values quoted from several authoritative sources and carried as bands because the sources themselves disagree; (b) exact lever-rule arithmetic checked against the phase-boundary compositions the tool itself places, which needs no external data.
reference_citations: Callister-type textbook Fe-Fe3C diagram (see e.g. the lecture handout https://eng.utq.edu.iq/wp-content/uploads/sites/4/2019/09/phase-diagram.pdf and Metallurgy e-learning notes): eutectoid 727 C, eutectic 1147 C / 4.3 %C, peritectic 1493 C / 0.16-0.18 %C, alpha_max 0.022 %C, gamma_max 2.11-2.14 %C, Fe3C 6.67 %C, 912 / 1395 / 1538 C

ASM-type evaluation of the C-Fe system as reproduced by https://metallurgysite.com/learning/matFeCdiagram.php and https://mechcodex.com/calculators/materials/fe-fe3c-phase-diagram (cited to ASM Handbook Vol. 3, Alloy Phase Diagrams): peritectic 1495 C with L=0.53, delta=0.09, gamma=0.17 %C; eutectic 1148 C with L=4.3, gamma=2.08 %C; eutectoid 727 C, alpha_max 0.022 %C, gamma_max 2.14 %C, Fe3C 6.67 %C, 912 / 1395 / 1538 C

IspatGuru, "The Iron-Carbon Phase Diagram", https://www.ispatguru.com/the-iron-carbon-phase-diagram/ : eutectic 4.26 %C, eutectoid 0.76 %C at 727 C, gamma_max 2.14 %C at 1148 C, alpha_max 0.025 %C at 727 C, 910 / 1394 / 1538 C
Stoichiometry of Fe3C from IUPAC atomic weights (12.011 / (3*55.845 + 12.011) = 6.689 wt% C)
tolerance: Mass fractions are printed as (f*100).toFixed(1) %, so the fraction tolerance is the display resolution 5e-4 (0.05 percentage points); the lever-rule and mass-balance identities are exact arithmetic on the tool's own tie-line ends, which are located by bisecting its own phase-field labels to machine precision. That needs the raw value to reach the tool: the framework rewrites a number control to Math.round(v*1e6)/1e6 while committing an input event, so driving the page with input+change instead quantises a tie-line end to 5e-7 wt%C, which is still three orders inside this tolerance and moves no verdict. Invariant points are compared against a BAND spanned by several published sources (eutectoid 727 C / 0.76-0.77 %C, eutectic 1147-1148 C / 4.26-4.30 %C, peritectic 1493-1495 C / 0.16-0.17 %C, gamma_max 2.14 %C, alpha_max 0.022-0.025 %C, Fe3C 6.67-6.69 %C, 910-912 / 1394-1395 / 1538 C) with 0.005 wt% and 0.5 C slack for the probe; where the sources disagree by more than that the case is flagged, never failed. The A3-line-shape case is informational only.

cases.note: "Invariant reaction points" table row "Peritectic": δ + L → γ. Published values disagree between sources, so the reference is the band spanned by them: T in [1493,1495] C (sources {"CAL":1493,"ASM":1495}), C in [0.16,0.17] wt% (sources {"CAL":0.16,"ASM":0.17}).

"Invariant reaction points" table row "Eutectic": L → γ(2.14) + Fe₃C. Published values disagree between sources, so the reference is the band spanned by them: T in [1147,1148] C (sources {"CAL":1147,"ASM":1148,"ISP":1148}), C in [4.26,4.3] wt% (sources {"CAL":4.3,"ASM":4.3,"ISP":4.26}).

"Invariant reaction points" table row "Eutectoid": γ → α(0.022) + Fe₃C. Published values disagree between sources, so the reference is the band spanned by them: T in [727,727] C (sources {"CAL":727,"ASM":727,"ISP":727}), C in [0.76,0.77] wt% (sources {"CAL":0.76,"ASM":0.77,"ISP":0.76}).

At the eutectoid temperature the alpha/(alpha+gamma) boundary is the maximum solubility of C in ferrite and the (alpha+gamma)/(gamma+Fe3C) boundary is the eutectoid composition. Boundaries are located by bisecting the tool's own phase-field labels at T = 727 C to 1e-8 wt%C. Reference bands come from the published source scatter.

At the eutectic temperature the gamma/(gamma+L) boundary is the maximum solubility of C in austenite and the (gamma+L)/(L+Fe3C) boundary is the eutectic composition. Boundaries are located by bisecting the tool's own phase-field labels at T = 1147 C to 1e-8 wt%C. Reference bands come from the published source scatter.

At the peritectic temperature the delta/(delta+L) boundary is the maximum solubility of C in delta ferrite and the (delta+L)/L boundary is the peritectic liquid composition. Boundaries are located by bisecting the tool's own phase-field labels at T = 1493 C to 1e-8 wt%C. Reference bands come from the published source scatter.

Right-hand edge of the diagram = the cementite composition. The textbook rounded value is 6.67 wt%C; exact Fe3C stoichiometry from IUPAC atomic weights gives 6.6897 wt%C, so the two references differ by 0.020 wt% (0.29 %).

cases.note: INFORMATIONAL (not a pass/fail physics test): the tool draws the A3 (GS) boundary as a straight line from 912 C at 0 wt%C to 727 C at 0.76 wt%C. Andrews (1965), JISI 203, 721-727, gives the independent empirical plain-carbon relation Ae3 = 910 - 203*sqrt(%C), which is strongly concave. The two published representations differ by up to 44.1 C in the middle of the range, far more than any display tolerance, so per the harness rule this is FLAGGED as a reference disagreement and a disclosed simplification, not scored as an error. Marked pass so it does not distort the score.

INFORMATIONAL: the alloy classifier snaps to "Eutectoid steel / 100 % pearlite" over |C - 0.76| < 0.015, but the test is applied AFTER the hypoeutectoid test, so the band is one-sided: 0.760-0.774 wt%C is called eutectoid while 0.745-0.759 wt%C is still called hypoeutectoid and gets a fraction (e.g. 0.750 wt%C -> 98.6 % pearlite, 1.4 % proeutectoid ferrite). The published eutectoid composition itself scatters over 0.76-0.80 wt%C, so this is flagged, not failed.
